title: Harden an nginx Config: TLS, Limits, and an Exposed Admin Area
intro: A security review flagged this server block. It works, which is how configurations like it survive for years: obsolete TLS versions, the nginx version advertised to scanners, a login form with no rate limit, an admin area open to the internet, and a directory listing over the uploads folder. Fix all of it without changing where anything is proxied.

steps.hint: limit_req_zone goes outside the server block (it belongs to the http level). In /admin/ the order matters: 'allow 10.20.0.0/16;' first, then 'deny all;', because the first matching rule wins. Delete the 'autoindex on;' line (or set it to off). Quote the HSTS value: add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000" always;
steps.fake_output:
nginx: the configuration file /etc/nginx/nginx.conf syntax is ok
nginx: configuration file /etc/nginx/nginx.conf test is successful
steps.explanation: The same routing as before, with each finding from the review closed.
steps.why: In the order of the task. (1) and (6): 5 requests a minute per address on the login form makes password guessing impractical, while burst=5 with nodelay lets a person retry a mistyped password without waiting; 429 instead of the default 503 tells clients and dashboards it was a limit, not an outage. Behind a load balancer the key must be the real client address, or the limit applies to everyone at once (webservers-incident-006). (2) TLS 1.0 and 1.1 have known weaknesses and are refused by current browsers and by compliance standards such as PCI DSS. (3) server_tokens off removes the version from headers and error pages, so scanners can't match it against a list of vulnerabilities; it hides the number, it doesn't patch anything. (4) HSTS makes returning browsers use HTTPS without first asking over HTTP; 'always' adds it to error responses too. It's hard to undo, so begin with a short max-age on a real site. Remember that an add_header inside a location replaces all the inherited ones. (5) The 1 MB default is too small for many apps and unlimited is an invitation to fill the disk; choose a number. (7) allow before deny, because the first match wins. A network restriction beats a login page alone, since the admin application's own flaws are no longer reachable. (8) autoindex turned the uploads folder into a browsable list of every file customers ever uploaded. Also make sure uploaded files can never be executed: no PHP or CGI handler may match that path.
